## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, that mention Idris. None is used in this draft.
- The inventory range of Idris is 19:56-57 and 21:85-86, which are all used. The verses 21:85-86 name Ismail and Dhul-Kifl as well, and the inventory also lists 38:48 under their events; the draft uses 21:85-86 only for what they say of Idris and leaves the event link empty because the chapter also cites 19:56-57.
- The sense of a high place (19:57) and of siddiq (19:56) is left open, and the draft does not say whether the raising was a rank or a place.
- The Quran gives no events of his life. The draft is short on purpose and a reviewer should not expect more from these verses.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of Idris with Enoch. It is not used in the story texts.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Idris in the Quran  (`#idris-in-the-quran`)

Cited ayat: 19:56-57, 21:85-86

> **19:56** وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِدْرِيسَ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا
>
> **19:57** وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا

> **21:85** وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
>
> **21:86** وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (19:56): The Quran tells its hearer to mention Idris in the scripture, and says that he was a siddiq, a word for someone of great truthfulness, and a prophet.

**c2** (19:57): God raised Idris to a high place.

**c3** (21:85): The Quran names Idris together with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl and says that each of them was among the patient.

**c4** (21:86): God admitted them into His mercy, and the Quran says that they were among the righteous.

### One-minute summary

The Quran tells its hearer to mention Idris, and says that he was a siddiq and a prophet [c1]. God raised him to a high place [c2]. The Quran names him with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl, each among the patient [c3].

### Complete story

The Quran tells its hearer to mention Idris in the scripture, and says that he was a siddiq, a word for someone of great truthfulness, and a prophet [c1]. God raised Idris to a high place [c2].

In another passage the Quran names Idris together with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl and says that each of them was among the patient [c3]. God admitted them into His mercy, and the Quran says that they were among the righteous [c4].

### Deep study

These passages say little and give no events [c1][c2][c3]. The first speaks of Idris by descriptions and an act of God: he was a siddiq and a prophet, and God raised him to a high place [c1][c2]. The later one names him in a group and gives the same descriptions to all of them: patient and righteous [c3][c4].

### Kids mode

The Quran tells us to remember Idris [c1]. It says he was truthful and a prophet [c1]. God raised him to a high place [c2]. The Quran also says that Idris, Ismail and Dhul-Kifl were each among the patient [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran presents Idris through his qualities, truthfulness and patience, and through what God did for him [c1][c2][c3]. Another is that being admitted into God's mercy is told of him together with others [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: when or where Idris lived, who his family was, what he said or did, or how long he lived. The Quran gives no events of his life.
- Not established: what a high place means in 19:57, whether a rank or a place; the verse says only that God raised him to a high place.
- Not established: the exact sense of the Arabic word siddiq beyond great truthfulness.
- Not established: in what way each of them was patient (21:85); the verse names them and gives no events.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of Idris with a figure called Enoch, and the stories told about his life. None is used in the story texts.
